newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Osem expects Nestle to raise stake.
newsitem.headline: Osem expects Nestle to raise stake.

text.p: Dan Propper, managing director and chief executive of Osem Investments, said he expects Nestle will increase its stake in the Israeli company to more than 50 percent.
"Nestle eventually will take control of Osem," Propper told Reuters. He said the Swiss giant would likely buy from the founding families shares in Osem when they become available.
Nestle owns 39.7 percent of Osem, Israel's second-largest publicly traded food manufacturer.

Salomon Brothers analyst Victor Halpert said in a report this month that in the long term Nestle may acquire the shares held by the founding families and even try to delist Osem's shares. The original founding families own 45 percent, Halpert said.
Propper said he did not believe Nestle intended to delist Osem.
Osem has exclusive rights to produce and market Nestle products in Israel.
